author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Restore selected EmuCoreX data from Google Drive safely
summary: Check the Drive account, backup date and selected categories. Keep a separate recovery copy, then verify progress using a normal in-game save.
heroAlt: Original illustration of selected backup categories moving from a cloud archive into local storage

blocks.text: Use a build with Google Drive backup support, an internet connection and enough free storage. Finish saving inside the game, then close emulation. Copy the current memory cards and other important data to a separate safe location. The profile settings cloud and Google Drive are separate services. Check the connected Drive account even if you already signed into your profile.

Open Google Drive backup from settings or the profile cloud dialog. Check the account and wait for the backup list to load. Select a completed backup with the expected date and device name. If the list is empty, check the account and connection first. Avoid creating or deleting backups repeatedly while diagnosing the missing entry.

Review the categories before confirming. Settings, memory cards, save states, cheats, patches, appearance and optional textures contain different data. A restored memory card can overwrite newer progress at the same destination. Select only what you need. Games, BIOS files, caches and sign-in data are excluded. On a new device, also check the local paths to your game folders.

Wait for restoration to finish before starting emulation or another backup. Start a familiar game normally and load a save from its memory card. Check your progress, controller behavior and restored settings. Test save states separately because compatibility can depend on the emulator build. Keep the recovery copy until you have checked your important games.
Recover from a wrong choice or an error

If progress is wrong, stop before saving over it. Restore your separate recovery copy or choose the correct backup. Reconnect the intended account after an authentication error. Quota errors require space on Drive; local storage errors require space on the device. Disconnecting Drive stops automatic backups but keeps remote copies. Do not delete remote copies to fix a local restoration problem.
